notes: Gate clearance and bridge repair are independent, absent by default and have no producer.
The southern checkpoint is a separate future land corridor; the damaged south-town road bends west before the southern wall.
Rivers meet each end of both walls. No playable shoreline, delta, named next town or original temple location is introduced.
Environment pass gives roads a hierarchy, farmyards explicit clear approaches and smaller crop parcels; added visual setpieces do not introduce quests or destination scenes.

adaptation: Preserve the inhabited corridor between western and eastern north-south waterways, woodland north, Greyfold foothills east, and cultivated riverlands south.
The runtime corridor widens and bends the atlas topology for 24px miniature-scale travel; no literal PNG scaling or uniform map-to-kilometre conversion is used.
The village brook and controlled millrace remain distinct local water features in detailed Eldenmere; they are not additional bounding rivers.
Neither boundary watercourse is assigned a new proper name or automatically identified as the River Leth. Repeated labels do not create duplicate rivers.
The old ridge sanctuary and original sacrificial temple receive no new location. Exact confluences, political borders, physical distances and unnamed settlements remain open.
North and south walls, checkpoints, walking loops, overlooks and bridge damage are authored runtime interpretation, not features redrawn onto the approved classroom map.

environment_pass.description: Authored farmsteads, working roads, layered woodland and regional-scale wayside details.
environment_pass.scale: Regional miniatures; fields and scenery convey place, not a physical kilometre scale.
